problem_statement: ShopGrids is a directly runnable static commerce landing page built with Bootstrap grid markup, one local stylesheet, local product images, a hero carousel, collection cards, best-seller product cards, a statistics band, a newsletter signup, and a footer, already rebranded into the fictional heritage travel-bag label "Marlowe & Field". Wire a shared "Field cart bar" purchase-continuity surface across the storefront: a slim basket summary with a live "Bag (N)" badge that appears in the navbar, beside the best-seller workshop grid, and in the service strip above the footer, plus an "Add to bag" button on the first workshop card that increments the basket so every badge re-renders "Bag (1)". The cart bar must reuse the existing heritage yellow/green palette and rounded card language, the product grid must keep a stable wrapping 2-up rhythm on 390px mobile with no horizontal overflow, and the storefront must remain a single static Bootstrap page with local assets only.
required_content: Keep the static HTML/CSS/Bootstrap architecture; do not add a framework, build tool, package manager, backend, remote API, remote image, generated screenshot, new asset file, or new dependency.
Add a shared Field cart bar (basket summary with a Bag (N) badge) that appears in the navbar, beside the best-seller workshop grid, and in the service strip above the footer.
Add an Add to bag button on the first workshop product card that increments the basket so every Field cart bar badge re-renders Bag (1) after a click.
The Field cart bar and its badge reuse the existing heritage yellow/green palette, rounded containers, and card language rather than a detached off-palette chrome.
Keep the four original local seller images assets/images/products/Sellers_1.png, Sellers_2.png, Sellers_3.png, and Sellers_4.png visible in the best-seller grid.

Preserve the navbar, hero carousel, collection cards, best-seller cards, statistics band, newsletter form, service strip, footer columns, local logo/brand/product images, and static HTTP serving behavior.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile captures must not show horizontal overflow, clipped headings, or unstable card widths; the workshop product grid keeps a wrapping 2-up rhythm on mobile.
design_constraints: Fit the existing source conventions: keep changes in index.html, assets/css/main.css, and assets/js/main.js, use Bootstrap container/row/col classes, and reuse the existing CSS variable palette such as --yalow, --green, --mix_gray, --mix_white2, and --_20_px.
The Field cart bar should read as part of the heritage store: yellow/green language, rounded pill badge, consistent on the navbar, workshop, and service-strip surfaces.

The add-to-bag interaction must genuinely update the shared basket state so every Field cart bar badge shows Bag (1); a handler that only toggles a button class without re-rendering the badge is incorrect.
Use stable dimensions such as aspect-ratio, bounded card body height, responsive wrapping, and normal CSS media queries; do not rely on viewport-width font scaling or hidden-only text.
Do not remove the carousel, collection cards, seller cards, statistics/newsletter/footer sections, edit vendor libraries, or replace local assets with placeholders.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial verify that the storefront shell loads responsively with the Field cart bar in the navbar.

desktop_catalog_layout, tablet_catalog_layout, and mobile_catalog_layout verify that the Field cart bar and workshop rail render in the heritage palette inside #sellers across breakpoints without horizontal overflow.
desktop_product_grid_regression verifies that the seller product cards, local Sellers images, heart controls, and bag controls remain present.
desktop_collection_footer_regression verifies that the Field cart bar also appears in the service strip above the footer and that the statistics, newsletter, and footer content remain reachable.
desktop_add_to_cart clicks the first workshop card Add to bag button and verifies every Field cart bar badge re-renders Bag (1).

Baseline capture should complete because new selectors are optional; absence of the footer cart bar, an off-palette bar, or a mobile grid overflow should be scored as failing dom/visual/responsive checks rather than an infrastructure failure.

change_completion: The Field cart bar (basket summary with a Bag (N) badge) appears in the navbar, beside the best-seller workshop grid, and in the service strip above the footer.
The first workshop card exposes an Add to bag button and every Field cart bar badge re-renders Bag (1) after a genuine click.
design_consistency: The Field cart bar reuses the heritage yellow/green palette, rounded pill badge, and card language rather than a detached off-palette charcoal chrome.
The cart bar and workshop rail read as part of the original storefront component across the navbar, workshop, and footer surfaces.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states show the cart bar and product grid without horizontal overflow or clipped headings.
The best-seller product grid keeps a stable wrapping 2-up rhythm on mobile with readable text and tappable controls.
regression: The navbar, hero carousel, collection cards, best-seller cards, statistics band, newsletter, service strip, footer columns, and local product/logo assets remain present.
The heart and bag controls remain in the seller cards and local Sellers_1.png through Sellers_4.png images remain browser-visible.

scoring_notes: A correct patch wires a shared Field cart bar purchase-continuity surface (basket summary + Bag (N) badge) across the navbar, best-seller workshop grid, and service strip, adds an Add-to-bag button on the first workshop card that increments the basket so every badge re-renders Bag (1), reuses the heritage yellow/green palette, and keeps a wrapping 2-up product grid on mobile with no horizontal overflow, all scoped to index.html, assets/css/main.css, and assets/js/main.js on the static Bootstrap page with local assets. A patch that drops the footer cart bar, collapses the workshop product grid so the cards overlap and clip or leaves the promise rail illegible, leaves the badge stale after add-to-bag, or overflows the mobile product grid should fail dom_assertions, visual_regression, interaction_assertions, or no_horizontal_overflow.
author_notes: Slot 306 (product-grade L4) targets the ShopGrids static commerce template rebranded to Marlowe & Field for commerce / implementation continuity / modify / cross_section. The reference wires the Field cart bar across the navbar, workshop, and footer surfaces with a working add-to-bag basket, in the heritage palette, with a clean mobile grid. The baseline carries the original defects (off-palette bar, missing footer bar, fixed-wide mobile grid overflow) but keeps a working badge sync (fails no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, dom_assertions; passes interaction). The bad solution ships a genuinely broken workshop - a compact-catalog refactor that collapses the product grid so the cards overlap and clip and leaves the promise rail illegible - and a stale-closure add-to-bag handler that flips the button state without re-rendering the badge, so it fails all four orthogonal gates.
